item.title: Zcash activates NU7 upgrade, freezing ≈$16M in oldest privacy pool – Link Zcash'
item.description:
Zcash activates NU7 upgrade, freezing ≈$16M in oldest privacy pool – Link

Zcash's NU7 network upgrade went live, invalidating version-4 transactions and making roughly 12,224 ZEC (≈$15-16M) in the legacy "Sprout" privacy pool unspendable. It also cut block times to roughly a third of previous levels.

The upgrade is a major technical migration for a top-20 privacy coin and may affect throughput, fee dynamics, and legacy fund access.

item.description:
Base mainnet ships denim upgrade, cutting block time to 200ms – Link

Base's fourth independent network upgrade went live on mainnet, shortening block intervals to 200 milliseconds and disabling Flashblocks.

Faster block times can improve transaction finality on one of the largest L2s and support higher-frequency DeFi and trading activity.

item.title: Democrats win full control of Congress, raising crypto regulatory uncertainty –
item.description:
Democrats win full control of Congress, raising crypto regulatory uncertainty – Link

Democrats retook both the House and Senate in the US midterms. Crypto-friendly Republicans Bryan Steil, Zach Nunn, and Ann Wagner lost seats, while Sherrod Brown is back in the Senate and Elizabeth Warren and Maxine Waters are positioned for key committee roles.

This lowers the odds of the market-structure/CLARITY Act passing in an industry-friendly form and may point to tighter scrutiny on stablecoins and digital-asset policy.

item.title: North Korean hackers continue laundering $6.3B Binance hack proceeds via THORCha
item.description:
North Korean hackers continue laundering $6.3B Binance hack proceeds via THORChain – Link

The FBI formally attributed the Oct 29 Binance hack to the TraderTraitor group, which has routed stolen SOL and ETH into BTC largely through THORChain swaps. Arkham data says about 81% of stolen SOL moved via the protocol, while Binance says it has restored ≈98% of affected user funds using company reserves.

DeFi cross-chain infrastructure is still hard to police even after attribution, and could increase pressure for address-blocking on THORChain-like protocols.

item.title: DTCС's tokenization service goes live with Morgan Stanley, JPMorgan, Citi, BofA
item.description:
DTCС's tokenization service goes live with Morgan Stanley, JPMorgan, Citi, BofA among first users – Link

Morgan Stanley confirmed it is using DTCC's newly launched DTS platform, live since Oct 28, to tokenize US stocks, ETFs, and Treasuries on-chain. The rollout includes about 20 institutions and runs on the Canton Network and DTCC's private Besu network.

• Coverage includes Russell 1000 constituents and major ETFs.
• Other users include JPMorgan, Citigroup, Bank of America, Fidelity, and Citadel Securities.

The institutional tokenization infrastructure is moving from pilot to real use and could support longer-term on-chain settlement adoption.

item.title: Binance attack traced to fake job interviews and a compromised AI coding tool –
item.description:
Binance attack traced to fake job interviews and a compromised AI coding tool – Link

Binance's investigation found attackers planted a tampered Homebrew package via a fake AI programming tool in June, then used a fake recruiter/interview scheme in September to compromise a second engineer's device. The exploit ultimately used Ethereum's EIP-7702 authorization mechanism to gain partial hot-wallet control.

It shows a multi-month social-engineering plus AI-tooling attack vector that exchanges and custodians may need to audit against.

The regulatory outcome could shape whether major DeFi vault products face securities registration requirements.

item.description:
THORChain drops on regulatory and security risk concerns tied to Binance hack laundering – Link

RUNE fell roughly 20% and briefly dipped below $0.50 after on-chain data showed North Korean hackers laundered about $42.7M in stolen Binance funds through THORChain's cross-chain swaps. US agencies have requested node operators block related flows, but co-founders have resisted address-freezing.

It highlights the tension between DeFi censorship resistance and regulatory pressure, which could affect RUNE's risk premium and liquidity.

item.description:
Binance raises market maker rebates to defend liquidity after record hack – Link

Bloomberg says Binance is offering temporary higher rebates to Tier 2/3 market makers, matching Tier 4 rates for one week after Bitcoin order book depth on the exchange fell about 30% within a 1% price range.

It is a direct attempt to stop liquidity flight and spread widening, and its effectiveness will show whether Binance can hold market share.

A proposed XRPL amendment enabling token-level permissioning has support from 33 of 35 trusted validators and is expected to activate this week. A related proposal to restrict unauthorized token holders remains under separate review.

This could change how issuers manage compliance and access controls on XRPL, especially for institutional and RWA use cases.

item.description:
Binance hack now largest crypto security incident on record, dragging October losses to $6.48B industry-wide – Link

PeckShield data shows 56 major security incidents in October 2026 totaling about $6.48B in losses, a 745% monthly surge. The Binance breach alone accounted for the bulk, with the FBI attributing the attack to North Korea's TraderTraitor group.

The scale of losses may keep risk-off sentiment elevated across CEXs and DeFi and could prompt tighter regulatory scrutiny of exchange custody practices.

item.title: INFINIT opens its second APEX vault – Link The team opened deposits for APEX 2 o
item.description:
INFINIT opens its second APEX vault – Link

The team opened deposits for APEX 2 on Oct 28, following the completion of its first 90-day trading vault on Hyperliquid.

During APEX 1, the team managed to achieve a 35% APR and outperformed all traditional indices like the S&P 500, KOSPI, HSE, etc.

INFINIT also provides access to onchain trading activity and weekly performance reports, allowing users to see how their funds were managed throughout the first round.

APEX 2 brings back the same managers, who plan to apply the same successful strategy, further benefiting from the data and live trading experience of the past three months.

Deposits close on Nov 11.

A successful second round could help establish APEX as a serious option for users looking to access professionally managed trading strategies.

item.title: Aave freezes 292 reserves across Aave V3/V4 within 90 minutes of Binance hack re
item.description:
Aave freezes 292 reserves across Aave V3/V4 within 90 minutes of Binance hack reaching its markets – Link

Aave's guardian multisigs froze 175 reserves across 16 networks on Aave V3 and 117 reserves on V4 after a Binance exploiter deposited 60M USDT and borrowed about 19,762 WETH (≈$44.6M) through the protocol. Markets have since reopened, but nine assets remain at zero LTV as a precaution.

The rapid response may support confidence in DeFi risk management, but it also shows that "immutable" protocols still rely on emergency intervention powers.

A wallet linked to the Binance hacker sold millions of UNI tokens on-chain, including dumping $5M of PROM for only $71 in ETH in a thin pool. UNI still gained roughly 3% over 24 hours.

Underlying demand, partly tied to Uniswap's expanding TJAR fee-conversion program across seven chains, is outweighing sell pressure for now.

item.title: Institutional investors pull funds from exchanges, spot ETFs show mixed flows –
item.description:
Institutional investors pull funds from exchanges, spot ETFs show mixed flows – Link

Following the Binance hack, institutional investors accelerated withdrawals from centralized exchanges more broadly, not just Binance. BTC spot ETFs saw a 4th straight day of modest net inflows (+$17.2M on Oct. 29), while ETH ETFs recorded continued outflows (-$105.5M on Oct. 29).

The divergence shows institutional risk appetite was already cooling in ETH before the exchange shock, which could pressure ETH relative to BTC near term.

item.title: Canton Strategic Holdings plans first SEC-compliant tokenized US stock trading o
item.description:
Canton Strategic Holdings plans first SEC-compliant tokenized US stock trading on Nov. 2 – Link

Nasdaq-listed Canton Strategic Holdings (CNTN) announced a deal with tokenized securities venue TSV to trade its own common stock in issuer-initiated tokenized form starting as early as Nov. 2. The company aims to be the first compliant onshore tokenized US equity trade under the SEC's Innovation Exemption Framework.

• Tokenized shares carry the same rights as Nasdaq shares.
• Trading will happen via an AMM for near 24/7 settlement.

If the launch proceeds smoothly, it could set a template for other issuers and signal early regulatory traction for tokenized equities in the US.

item.title: Polymarket front-end exploit adds to risk-off sentiment alongside Binance hack –
item.description:
Polymarket front-end exploit adds to risk-off sentiment alongside Binance hack – Link

Separately from Binance, Polymarket users reported unauthorized asset transfers and suspicious withdrawal signature requests on Oct. 29, suspected to be a front-end attack. One user alone reported an $800K loss, and Polymarket has not yet confirmed the cause.

Standard Chartered said the Binance hack plus the Polymarket exploit could keep crypto under pressure before a base is found. The cluster of security incidents may be eroding confidence in platform security.
